title: When the gateway cannot finish
goal: {{castAgentId}} at {{castBrand}} calls a permitted tool while the gateway's upstream is down.
obstacle: A failure looks like a refusal if you only read the status. A client must tell "the policy said no" from "nothing answered".
control: The lab arms a one-shot simulated 502. The verdict is Upstream error: a connection problem, not a policy decision, and the error text is shown in full in the verdict pane as JSON, never as an HTML error page.
say: This is not a refusal. Nothing was decided, because nothing answered.

steps.title: Arm the failure and run
steps.tell: Choose the upstream-error scenario (labelled simulated) and run list_entitlements. The verdict is Upstream error.
steps.say: A connection failure, named as one.
steps.why: Rule: a downstream failure is always named, never a blank page or an empty 200.

steps.title: Run it again
steps.tell: Run it again without the scenario. The fault was one-shot, so the call now succeeds.
steps.say: Same call, different outcome, because the cause was the connection.
steps.why: Telling a transient fault from a policy refusal is the point of the verdict word.
